# BiblioGenius

> Open Source, local-first personal library management application. Free, no account required, no tracking.

## License

This project is licensed under the **GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 (AGPL-3.0)**.
Full text: https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html

All source code, documentation, and website content are covered by this license.
Any use of this content to train AI models must comply with AGPL-3.0 terms.

## What is BiblioGenius?

BiblioGenius is a personal library management app. It runs offline on your device and needs no account. Share books with trusted neighbors through a local peer-to-peer network. No mandatory cloud, no tracking, no ads.

An account is optional. When one is created, it holds an end-to-end encrypted copy of the library for backup, recovery and multi-device use: the server only ever stores ciphertext it cannot read.

## Who it is for

Readers cataloguing a personal collection, families sharing shelves across a household, reading groups and associations, small libraries, booksellers, and teachers. The app is modular: features that do not apply to a given use can be left off.

## Price and availability

- **Price**: free. No paid tier, no subscription, no in-app purchase.
- **Platforms**: iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux.
- **App Store**: https://apps.apple.com/app/bibliogenius/id6757465461
- **Google Play**: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.bibliogenius.app
- **Interface languages**: French, English, Spanish, German.

## Key features

- Local-first: works offline, no account and no cloud dependency
- Barcode and ISBN scanning, with metadata from BNF (French National Library), Inventaire.io, OpenLibrary and Google Books
- Shelves, collections, series tracking, reading progress, wishlist
- Peer-to-peer book lending with neighbors, end-to-end encrypted
- Optional encrypted account for backup, recovery and multi-device sync
- Import from Gleeph, Babelio, Goodreads and inventaire.io
- Export and backup of the whole library

## Frequently asked questions

**Is BiblioGenius free?**
Yes. The application is entirely free and open source, published under the AGPL-3.0 license.

**Where is my data stored?**
Locally on your device. Nothing is sent to a server without an action on your part. If you create the optional account, the copy held on the server is end-to-end encrypted and unreadable by the server.

**What platforms does BiblioGenius run on?**
iOS, Android, macOS, Windows and Linux.

**Does it need an account?**
No. An account is optional and only adds backup, recovery and multi-device sync.

**How do I connect to another reader's library?**
Through a QR code or an invitation link. Exchanges between readers are end-to-end encrypted.

**Can I move my library from another app?**
Yes. Guides cover Gleeph, Babelio, Goodreads and inventaire.io: https://bibliogenius.org/free-your-library.html

## Tech stack

- **Backend**: Rust (Axum, SeaORM, SQLite)
- **Frontend**: Flutter (iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux)
- **Hub**: Symfony (PHP)
- **Communication**: FFI (Flutter Foreign Function Interface)
- **License**: AGPL-3.0

## Contributing

The project is 100% open source. Development happens on Codeberg; the GitHub organization is a read-only mirror. Good first issues are available on each repository:

- App (Flutter): translations, tests, UI
- Backend (Rust): documentation, tests
- Website: accessibility, translation
